prompt: Create one high fidelity native Android app UI design concept, portrait 432x960 screen, flat straight-on screen artwork with no phone hardware, no perspective, no surrounding presentation board. MenetrendGO, a Hungarian MÁV timetable and vehicle tracking app. Operate mode, effortlessly clear commuter tool. User-pinned aesthetic: fully rounded, slightly liquid-glassed, quiet cool pale icy blue background #EDF4FA, deeply legible midnight blue #112D43, restrained royal blue #2864D9 action, broad generous whitespace, subtle translucent blue-white panels with luminous upper edges and gentle offset soft shadows, never heavy blur or shiny toy chrome. Native Material 3 anatomy, Roboto, accessible readable type, 48dp controls, coherent thin rounded outline icons. Status bar 9:41. Four labeled bottom navigation destinations exactly: Tervezés, Térkép, Bérletek, Beállítások, Tervezés selected; rounded floating translucent navigation with system gesture bar below. Header MenetrendGO and small profile-free notification bell. Exact Hungarian typography as far as possible. Clear primary action 'Járatok keresése'. Fields 'Honnan?' and 'Hová?' have selected values 'Mór, autóbusz-állomás' and 'Székesfehérvár'. A swap icon button beside fields; date/time control 'Ma, indulás most'. Below form show sample route 20:15 → 21:01, 46 perc, Közvetlen, bus route 8097, a small pass chip 'Bérlet: ellenőrzés szükséges'. Label sample results 'Szemléltető adatok' subtly but legibly. No prices, no official logo, no advertisements, no invented features, no English UI labels. Show entire usable app screen at sharp resolution. Layout C guided journey: Main title 'Merre tovább?' and two separate large full-width milky rounded station controls with tiny linked vertical origin-destination line between left icons. Date/time row below, wide blue rounded 'Járatok keresése'. Generous separation then 'A következő utad' with one wide low glass route preview: origin and destination aligned vertically on left, times 20:15 and 21:01 on right; 8097 and Közvetlen at bottom, small pass chip. Screen feels like a simple travel companion, not a dashboard. No extra navigation.
